title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang missing from Time's 100 most influential people in AI list for 2026
article:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company has become one of the biggest suppliers of chips powering the artificial intelligence boom, has been left off Time magazine's 2026 list of the 100 most influential people in AI. The omission has drawn attention because Jensen Huang featured on the list in each of its first three editions, starting in 2023. The 2026 list includes several prominent figures from technology, business and entertainment, including Elon Musk , OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Time says its annual list recognises people who are shaping the key developments in artificial intelligence and influencing the technology's growth.
Jensen Huang missing from Time 100 AI 2026 list
Jensen Huang's absence stands out given Nvidia's central role in the AI industry. The company's graphics processing units, or GPUs, are widely used to train and run advanced AI systems, making Nvidia a major player in the rapid growth of the sector. Notably, Jensen Huang was included in Time's AI 100 lists in 2023, 2024 and 2025. However, he does not appear on the 2026 list. Time described the purpose of its list as identifying people who “best represent the year’s key storylines” and who are having the most influence on developments in AI.
Elon Musk, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei appear in the list
Several of the biggest names in AI are featured on this year's list. These include SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. The list also includes executives and leaders associated with companies including IBM, Google DeepMind, ByteDance, Broadcom, Databricks, Amazon and Oracle. Beyond technology leaders, the 2026 list also features names from entertainment and politics, including Ben Affleck, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Paris Hilton and US Senator Bernie Sanders. Time 100 AI list highlights changing influence in AI Time's list is not a ranking of companies or a direct measure of business success. Instead, the publication selects people it believes have had significant influence on the major AI developments of the year. As a result, the list changes from year to year and can include researchers, business leaders, policymakers and public figures alongside technology executives.
